//: Lighthouse CI budgets (plan/01 §7, spec 004 AC-24). JSON has no comments, so this key is the
note; `@lhci/cli` reads `.ci` and ignores everything beside it.
**This job blocks since TASK-056.** `continue-on-error` is gone from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
the URL set is the five of AC-24 (`tests/fixtures/seo/lighthouse-urls.json`), and every
assertion below is an `error`. What made the flip possible was not a schedule but two
decisions TASK-056 was asked to take, both recorded here because the numbers are meaningless
without them.
**1. Where it measures: this repository's own bytes, Brotli-encoded.** The job builds, runs
`next start`, puts `scripts/seo/brotli-origin.ts` in front of it and points Lighthouse at the
proxy — it no longer measures a Vercel preview. `resource-summary:script:size` is **transfer**
size, i.e. the bytes on the wire after content encoding, and neither available origin sent the
bytes this budget is written in: `next start` negotiates gzip (the same build reads 148 298 B
gzip and 124 314 B Brotli, so a compliant page fails a Brotli budget measured over gzip —
`/review 53`'s finding), and a protected preview sends Brotli but injects `vercel.live`, the
platform's preview-feedback script, which is 25 376 B on `/` and ~48 KB on a locale document,
is absent from production and is in no build output of ours. A budget a platform script can
blow is not a budget this repository can hold. Measured against the Brotli origin, the number
here and the number `pnpm budget:client-js` prints from `.next/` are the same number, and both
are what an edge CDN serves.
**2. What the number is: 131 072 B (128 KB) of Brotli script transfer.** spec 004 §13 Q13
restated `plan/01` §7's 120 KB gzip as 120 KB Brotli (founder, 2026-09-08, option (a)) and
§14 A1 corrected it to 128 KB once TASK-046 measured the locale documents at 129 638 B with no
application code left to remove. It is not raised a second time (§14 A1). The measured numbers
at the flip: `/` 126 586 B, each locale document 128 045-129 298 B — 1 774 to 4 486 B of
headroom, all of it Next 16.3.4's runtime. **The GA4 tag does not fit in that headroom**: with
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GA4_MEASUREMENT_ID` set, `gtag.js` adds ~30-35 KB and this assertion fails. The
id is unset in CI, locally, on previews and in production (`docs/compliance/ropa.md` row 4),
so nothing measured here loads it; setting it is a RoPA-affecting act that also needs a budget
decision, and TASK-056 records that rather than pre-emptively widening the budget for a tag
nobody has switched on (spec 004 §14 A15).
`largest-contentful-paint` is asserted at 2 000 ms per `plan/01` §7. It was red on every locale
document until TASK-056: the LCP element was the consent sheet's body paragraph — an
`ssr: false` island, so it paints after hydration — which as one 187-character block was larger
than the hero heading. The body is two paragraphs now, the LCP element is the `H1` the page is
about, and `tests/e2e/lcp.spec.ts` fails if any overlay text block grows past it again.
**`/` has the thinnest margin in the set, and it is the origin rather than the page** (spec
004 §14 A18, `/review 61`). Warmed, over two passes, `/` reports 2 425 / 2 106 / 1 952 and
2 660 / 2 181 / 1 930 ms against the 2 000 ms above, while the four locale documents report
1 430-1 649. Its LCP element is the chooser's
intro paragraph and cannot be made the `H1` by any design-safe change — the `H1` is a single
380 x 30 px line, 11 560 px², against the paragraph's 33 943 px² — and it would not help: in a
browser `/` emits **one** LCP candidate at 112 ms, because it is SSG with no island to wait
for. What the number tracks is when the later of the two render-blocking stylesheets arrived
`/` is the *fastest* document in the set:
4 200 B of SSG served at ~20 ms, so its document, three font preloads, two stylesheets and
eight script chunks all queue at once against `scripts/seo/brotli-origin.ts`, which is plain
HTTP/1.1 with six connections and no multiplexing. Two things are recorded there and
deliberately not changed here: `@lhci/cli` defaults `aggregationMethod` to `optimistic`, so
this assertion is evaluated against the **fastest** of the three runs (`/`'s medians are
2 106 and 2 181 ms), and serving the measured build over HTTP/2 is what removes the queue.
Both are
gate-strength decisions for the founder/orchestrator, not a round-2 fix; the assertion itself
is not weakened.
`categories:seo` is collected but deliberately **not** asserted: every page in Phase 0 is
`noindex` (ADR-0007, spec 001 §6), so the SEO category would score the robots directive rather
than the page, and nobody should be able to make a number green by indexing early. Spec 007
asserts it when there is an indexable set.
